name: Ritvo Autism Asperger Diagnostic Scale, 14 item Screen
developer: Eriksson, Andersen and Bejerot (2013), Karolinska Institutet; derived from the RAADS-R (Ritvo et al., 2011)
construct: Autistic traits in adults, covering mentalizing deficits, social anxiety and sensory reactivity, with developmental timing captured in the response format.

instructions: Please answer the questions according to what is true for you. Check only one column per statement!

responseOptions.label: True now and when I was young
True only when I was younger than 16

items.text: It is difficult for me to understand how other people are feeling when we are talking
Some ordinary textures that do not bother others feel very offensive when they touch my skin
It is very difficult for me to work and function in groups
It is difficult to figure out what other people expect of me
I often don't know how to act in social situations
I can chat and make small talk with people
items.note: Reversed item: scored 0 for True now and when I was young through 3 for Never true

items.text: When I feel overwhelmed by my senses, I have to isolate myself to shut them down
How to make friends and socialize is a mystery to me
When talking to someone, I have a hard time telling when it is my turn to talk or to listen
Sometimes I have to cover my ears to block out painful noises (like vacuum cleaners or people talking too much or too loudly)
It can be very hard to read someone's face, hand, and body movements when we are talking
I focus on details rather than the overall idea
I take things too literally, so I often miss what people are trying to say
I get extremely upset when the way I like to do things is suddenly changed

scoring: Score each item 3 (true now and when I was young), 2 (true only now), 1 (true only when I was younger than 16) or 0 (never true); item 6 is reversed (0, 1, 2, 3). Sum for a total of 0 to 42; higher scores indicate more autistic traits. Eriksson et al. (2013): a cut off score of 14 or above gives sensitivity 0.97 and specificity 0.46 against ADHD, 0.64 against other psychiatric disorders and 0.95 against non psychiatric controls. A 5 item short form with cut off 4 or above out of 15 had sensitivity 0.93 and specificity 0.45 to 0.49 in the psychiatric samples. Screening tool only, not diagnostic.
citation: Eriksson, J. M., Andersen, L. M., & Bejerot, S. (2013). RAADS-14 Screen: Validity of a screening tool for autism spectrum disorder in an adult psychiatric population. Molecular Autism, 4(1), 49. https://doi.org/10.1186/2040-2392-4-49
transcriptionNote: Items transcribed from Table 2 ('The RAADS-14 Screen') of the PMC copy of the open access article (PMC3907126), with subscale membership from Tables 3 and 4 and item 6 marked as the only reversed item; item 10 was returned in two fragments and rejoined. The BMC article page itself returned only 2 item texts to WebFetch and the Additional file 1 (print version with clinician instructions) URL was not exposed. Response labels are quoted from the Methods description of the RAADS-R 4 point scale; Table 2's own label wording was not quoted and may differ slightly (the Swedish Region Kronoberg form phrases them as 'True for me now and when I was young', 'True only for me now', 'True only when I was young (before age 16)', 'Never true for me'). Normative medians by population were not transcribed. Second pass: response labels confirmed against Table 2 headers.
